about: The winds, woodwinds and brass, as a tree of types (registry/README.md; docs/WIND_TYPES.md): a family above each group of instruments that share how they are built and played, so that what they share is written once on the family -- here, a player's values (players/winds.json); in a table written by type, its entry, read through this tree by registry/registry.js `typed` and native/wind-types. Begun with what their players share: a vocal tract upstream of the reed, one model whose values are its players' -- measured of clarinettists, every reed player's until their own are measured. Their bodies are still render/synthesis/geometry's (research/REGISTRY_PLAN.md, the woodwinds' step).

wind.about: A wind instrument: a column of air in a bore, sounded by its player's breath. What every wind shares is written here once and taken by each type below through this tree (docs/WIND_TYPES.md): its air, its player's airway upstream of what sounds it (players/winds.json), and its entry in every table written by type.

woodwind.about: A wind whose notes are fingered on tone holes along its bore: its holes, their chimneys, pads and keywork, its fingering chart, the joints its player pulls to tune it (render/synthesis/geometry/tuning-points.json) and the points its makers adjust (geometry/making-points.json).

reed-woodwind.about: A woodwind sounded by a reed in the player's mouth: what the reed is driven by is the mouth's pressure less the tract's answer to the flow through it (native/openwind src/tract.rs).

single-reed.about: A reed woodwind whose one reed beats against the lay of a mouthpiece, its player's lower lip on the reed: its reed's law on its lay (render/synthesis/geometry/reed-lay.json), its mouthpiece's chamber and its tip's opening.

clarinet-family.about: A clarinet of any size: a bore cylindrical for most of its length and closed at its reed, sounding its odd resonances and overblowing a twelfth through a register vent. Every size is fingered and written alike, so what its makers and players tune it by is written once, here, in written notes, each size's sounding pitches its own transposition's; and what was measured of clarinettists was measured on the B-flat (Fritz & Wolfe 2005; Chen, Smith & Wolfe 2009), every size's until its own are measured.

clarinet.about: The B-flat clarinet, whose players' tracts were measured as they played (Fritz & Wolfe 2005; Chen, Smith & Wolfe 2009).

a-clarinet.about: The clarinet in A, a semitone below the B-flat and played on its mouthpiece and reed: its players' tract and laws the clarinettists' (measured on the B-flat) until its own are measured.

e-flat-clarinet.about: The E-flat clarinet: its players' tract the reed woodwinds' (the clarinettists' measured) until its own are measured.

basset-horn.about: The basset horn in F, a fourth below the B-flat clarinet, its compass carried down to written C3, with a crook and an upturned bell, narrower-bored than the alto clarinet beside it: its players' tract and laws the clarinettists' (measured on the B-flat) until its own are measured.

alto-clarinet.about: The alto clarinet in E-flat, a fifth below the B-flat, with a crook and an upturned bell: its players' tract and laws the clarinettists' (measured on the B-flat) until its own are measured.

bass-clarinet.about: The bass clarinet: its players' tract the reed woodwinds' (the clarinettists' measured) until its own are measured.

contra-alto-clarinet.about: The contra-alto clarinet in E-flat, an octave below the alto: its players' tract and laws the clarinettists' (measured on the B-flat) until its own are measured.

contrabass-clarinet.about: The contrabass clarinet in B-flat, an octave below the bass: its players' tract and laws the clarinettists' (measured on the B-flat) until its own are measured.

saxophone.about: A saxophone, whose players' tracts were measured as they played the tenor (Chen, Smith & Wolfe 2008, 2011): every saxophonist's until each size's own are measured.

soprano-saxophone.about: The soprano saxophone: its players' tract the saxophonists' (measured on the tenor) until its own are measured.

alto-saxophone.about: The alto saxophone: its players' tract the saxophonists' (measured on the tenor) until its own are measured.

tenor-saxophone.about: The tenor saxophone, whose players' tracts were measured as they played (Chen, Smith & Wolfe 2008, 2011).

baritone-saxophone.about: The baritone saxophone: its players' tract the saxophonists' (measured on the tenor) until its own are measured.

double-reed.about: A reed woodwind whose two blades beat against each other, held between its player's lips or (a capped reed) out of their reach, on a staple or a bocal: its reed's law the double reeds' (render/synthesis/reed-laws.json `doubleReeds`). Its bore is its own part: a cone's for an oboe, a bassoon or a shawm, a cylinder's for a duduk.

oboe-family.about: An oboe of any size: a narrow conical bore overblowing an octave, its reed on a staple (the oboe) or on a bocal (the English horn and the sizes below it).

oboe.about: The oboe, a double reed: its players' tract the reed woodwinds' (the clarinettists' measured) until its own are measured.

english-horn.about: The English horn, a double reed: its players' tract the reed woodwinds' (the clarinettists' measured) until its own are measured.

bassoon-family.about: A bassoon of any size: a long conical bore doubled back on itself, its reed on a bocal, its finger holes drilled aslant through a thick wall.

bassoon.about: The bassoon, a double reed: its players' tract the reed woodwinds' (the clarinettists' measured) until its own are measured.

contrabassoon.about: The contrabassoon, a double reed: its players' tract the reed woodwinds' (the clarinettists' measured) until its own are measured.

duduk.about: The duduk, the Armenian double reed: a short cylindrical bore of apricot wood, a large flattened reed, finger holes and a thumb hole and no keys -- a double reed on the bore a clarinet has, named here so that the tree holds one (docs/WIND_TYPES.md); nothing of it is measured or played yet, its players' tract and laws the reed woodwinds' (measured on clarinettists) until its own are measured.

shawm.about: The shawm, the oboe's forebear: a conical bore flaring to a wide bell, a double reed on a staple, finger holes -- named here so that the tree holds one (docs/WIND_TYPES.md); nothing of it is measured or played yet, its players' tract and laws the reed woodwinds' (measured on clarinettists) until its own are measured.

jet-woodwind.about: A woodwind sounded by its player's jet across an edge: its blowing pressure follows the note's frequency as flutists were measured blowing it (players/winds.json; Fletcher 1975).

alto-flute.about: The alto flute in G, the flute scaled to its bore (tools/design_openwind_woodwind.py flute_like): its players' law the flutists' until its own is measured.

piccolo.about: The piccolo in C, the flute scaled to its bore: its players' law the flutists' until its own is measured.

lip-reed.about: A brass instrument, sounded by its player's lips buzzing into its mouthpiece: the flow between them the reed's, its lips opening outward (native/openwind src/kernel.rs T_REED, T_LIPS). Its bodies are render/synthesis/geometry's (tools/save_brass_body.py).

trombone.about: The tenor trombone, its slide moving.

horn.about: The French horn, its bore a horn in F (Kemp 2002).

tuba.about: The tuba in C (an Alexander CC, Campbell et al. 2021).

reed-bore.about: The bore a reed drives, as a part of its instrument (`parts.bore`): what follows from its shape, whatever reed is on it, is written once on its kind here and taken by every instrument that names it -- in a table written by type, laid under what the instrument's own family writes (registry.js laidLine; native/wind-types laid_line). A reed's kind and a bore's are not one line: a clarinet and a duduk share the one, an oboe and a duduk the other.

reed-cylinder.about: A bore cylindrical for most of its length and closed at its reed: its lowest note a quarter wave of it, its odd resonances the strong ones, overblowing a twelfth -- a clarinet's of any size, and a duduk's.

reed-cone.about: A bore conical from near its reed, the cone's missing tip made up by its reed's and its staple's, bocal's or mouthpiece's volume: its lowest note a half wave of the whole cone, a full series of resonances, overblowing an octave -- an oboe's, a bassoon's, a saxophone's and a shawm's.
